newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo put limits on Hamanaka positions--witness.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo put limits on Hamanaka positions--witness.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp set limits in 1992 on copper warrant holdings by its copper team, then led by Yasuo Hamanaka, after allegations emerged that he was trying to manipulate world prices, a Sumitomo manager said on Monday.

Testifying at the second session of Hamanaka's trial for fraud and forgery, Yoshio Takeuchi, of Sumitomo's credit control department, said Sumitomo officials rejected repeated requests thereafter by Hamanaka to raise or remove the limits.

Takeuchi was called as a witness to shed light on Sumitomo's system of checks and controls, which Hamanaka's lawyers have said were lax and partly to blame for the trade house's $2.6 billion losses in the copper market.
